title: Implement an LRU cache in Go
description: Build a fixed-capacity LRU (Least Recently Used) cache in Go using a doubly-linked list and hash map. Tests are provided; implement internal/lru/lru.go to make them pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Create internal/lru/lru.go implementing a fixed-capacity LRU (Least Recently Used) cache.

The package is `lru` and must export:
  func New(cap int) *Cache            — create a cache with the given capacity
  func (c *Cache) Get(key string) (string, bool) — return value and true, or "", false if missing; accessing a key makes it most recently used
  func (c *Cache) Put(key, value string) — insert or update; if at capacity, evict the least recently used entry first
  func (c *Cache) Len() int           — number of entries currently stored
  func (c *Cache) Cap() int           — maximum capacity

Implementation hint: use a doubly-linked list + map[string]*node for O(1) get and eviction.

All 6 tests in internal/lru/lru_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: internal/lru/lru.go with Cache type and New/Get/Put/Len/Cap
Eviction removes LRU entry when at capacity
Get promotes accessed key to most-recently-used
Put on existing key updates value and promotes recency
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
